purpose: Visitor-facing blurbs for the left-panel POI tab. The viewer reads this file to attach short, person-readable copy to features that already exist on the map. Blurbs live here, not on the source GeoJSONs, so a re-export of buildings/cemeteries/publish data does not overwrite this content. Entries with blurb=null carry a revisit_note explaining what info is missing; the viewer surfaces those as 'info needed' placeholders so the gaps stay auditable in git instead of hiding as TODOs in code.
match_fields: Each entry matches a feature by `source` (which layer/dataset it lives in) plus one identifying property. Order in `entries` is the order rows render under each group when no other sort is applied.

groups.label: Buildings in the park
groups.note: Public park facilities from FEMA USA Structures footprints, AOP-confirmed (2026-06): 1010 Pavilion, 1033 rentable Farmhouse, 880 Front Office. Private residences on AOP land (665, 889) are intentionally not listed — they render as non-interactive black-box presence markers only.

groups.label: Trails
groups.note: Currently observed-ride evidence from the Saturday Afternoon GPX. Numbered-trail names/descriptions are being assembled in aop_trail_catalog.json (9 trails curated so far); they wire in here once real per-trail geometry is digitized. SFWDA paper-map numbered trails still owed; see brain/tasks/01_mvp/_done/community_trails_import.md.

groups.label: Cemeteries (in and around the park)
groups.note: Tennessee Comptroller parcel records, classed religious. Ellis is the AOP inholding; the other three sit in the 9-patch but outside the working envelope.

groups.label: Visitor support (off-park)
groups.note: Regional supply / lodging / fuel orientation. These already carry rich content in their GeoJSON properties; the index entries just point to a reading order.

groups.label: Drawn POIs (your edits)
groups.note: Per-browser localStorage. Visible only to the user who placed them; not shipped data.

entries.blurb: AOP Pavilion. The on-site building that hosts registration, awards, and the campfire. Footprint from FEMA structures data; AOP confirms it's the pavilion.
The Farmhouse — a public building on AOP land that can be rented. The 1033 Ellis Cove Road footprint; AOP-confirmed as the rentable farmhouse (2026-06).
The Front Office — public building at 880 Ellis Cove Road. AOP-confirmed (2026-06).
Ellis Cemetery — the AOP inholding. A 0.12-acre family cemetery carved out of the working envelope (the interior ring in the park boundary). Treat as private; stay clear of the parcel.

entries.revisit_note: Gilliam Cemetery sits in the 9-patch outside the AOP working envelope. Add visitor context once we know whether it is accessible from any AOP route and what the rider should know about it.
Bible Cemetery sits in the 9-patch outside the AOP working envelope. Same gap as Gilliam — accessibility and visitor relevance still owed.
Tate Cemetery sits in the 9-patch outside the AOP working envelope. Same gap as Gilliam / Bible.

entries.blurb: Closest supply town, 5-8 mi southeast (~10-15 min via Ellis Cove Road). Food, fuel, convenience, hotels, I-24 interchange. Chattanooga metro another ~30 mi for airport, big-box, and full city services.

The plateau cluster up the mountain — a second base after the South Pittsburg / Kimball run. Lodging at Smokehouse Lodge & Cabins or the Monteagle hotels; food at the Mountain Goat Market, the Smokehouse Restaurant, and High Point. Farther out, but a solid fallback when the closer side books up for the event.

entries.revisit_note: Per-row blurbs are not authored here — drawn POIs render their own category as the subtitle.
